title: McRae's big band at the Apollo for Schiffman
summary: Schiffman heard McRae's band rehearsing and booked it, with Ike Quebec and Eddie "Lockjaw" Davis on tenor.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you ever get involved with the Apollo music scene?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Oh, yeah. In '47. I went in there with that big band, yeah. (Every Inaudible) evening.
I really (inaudible) but he thought -- He say, "Where you get this band?" He came --
Schiffman came -- I was rehearsing downstairs right by that, (inaudible) downstairs. So he said, "I'm gonna let you bring your band in."
I say, "Okay, I'll bring my big band in." "Give me a price."
I say, "Okay, the price is good," you know. Scale for musicians. He didn't know I was gonna bring in like four trumpets and three trombones. Six saxophones with myself. Now I'm playing --
In this band was Ike Quebec and -- whatchacallem, tenor player?

Eddie's wanted to (inaudible) try to get his tone straightened out (inaudible). And these were two great tenor players back in those days. Ike Quebec was one of the finest, you know. Ike Quebec was real fine. That was -- people don't talk about him. Nobody really talk about that man, but he was really way up there on top. I put him up there -- Howk Benny and the (inaudible) class. For the type of playing he could do. He was good. He was really good. That time Lockjaw was getting his tone straightened out. They kid me about -- I let them play, so when I came in with this big band, I had, man oh (inaudible), it was outta sight! People heard it.
